.. change::
    :tags: bug, autogenerate

    Fixed autogenerate so that when the
    :paramref:`.EnvironmentContext.configure.target_metadata` parameter is
    a sequence of :class:`.MetaData` objects, the tables from all the
    objects are sorted by foreign key dependency as a single group.  A
    table in one :class:`.MetaData` that has a :class:`.ForeignKey` to a
    table in another :class:`.MetaData` is now created after its referent
    regardless of which :class:`.MetaData` object is listed first, so that
    the generated migration can actually be applied.  Previously the
    tables were sorted per :class:`.MetaData` object and then concatenated,
    so that an unexpected input order could produce a migration that
    failed because a referenced table did not yet exist; a cross-object
    reference could also raise ``NoReferencedTableError`` while the
    comparison was running.  The tables are still sorted by SQLAlchemy's
    own dependency sort, so a genuine foreign key cycle between tables
    continues to be handled by the existing dialect-aware logic and emits
    SQLAlchemy's usual cycle warning.

    The error raised for duplicate table keys across multiple
    :class:`.MetaData` objects now identifies the source
    :class:`.Table` objects, including the position of the
    :class:`.MetaData` object that contains each one.  A table that names
    the default schema explicitly is now treated as the same key as one
    that omits it.
